title: Pilot eval triage and guardrail tuning with Synthesis Solutions
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot evaluation results, investigate a regression spike in factuality scores on the payments prompt-set, adjust guardrail heuristics, and align on next steps for a targeted benchmark and security checklist. AE/SE reviewed recent eval spreadsheet, agreed on a bisect plan for prompt variants, and flagged a potential data residency question for Private deployment. Action owners assigned.
topics: prompt set pruning and scoring thresholds

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-16 09:00 PT
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Aisha Rahman (Synthesis Head of AI), Carlos Mendes (Synthesis ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Synthesis PM), Tom Liu (Synthesis Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok good morning everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync. quick agenda recap: evaluation results, regression triage, guardrail tuning and security questions. is that still right for everyone?
[00:20] Aisha Rahman: yep that looks good, i've got the evaluation spreadsheet open, saw the spike on the payments prompt, curious to hear your take.
[00:34] Jordan Patel: yeah we pulled the latest run — thanks for sending the runs.csv — we noticed the factuality F1 dropped from .87 to .72 specifically on the payments prompt-set, other sets were stable.
[00:48] Carlos Mendes: correct, we also saw an uptick in hallucinations where the model invents bank codes, sometimes spits out routing numbers, which is a big no for production.
[01:05] Maya Chen: uhh that's concerning. quick clarification — are those prompts that were edited in the UI last week, or the same canonical set?
[01:20] Priya Kapoor: we did add a few paraphrases to increase coverage, maybe 10% more variations. could that cause the drift?
[01:33] Jordan Patel: it's possible; paraphrases can expose model weaknesses in out-of-distribution phrasing. we'll want to do a bisect — run the eval on the original core set, then incremental additions to see the delta.
[01:48] Aisha Rahman: we can do that on our side but would appreciate if Redwood could run a controlled bisect with the same runtime config to isolate config vs data.
[02:03] Jordan Patel: absolutely, we can schedule that. quick note on runtime — were you using hosted with caching on? i see a caching flag in your config export.
[02:18] Carlos Mendes: yeah we enabled prefix caching last week to shave latency. the trial had a 10% throughput gain on average but i wonder if cache interactions change tokenization or context?
[02:33] Jordan Patel: cache shouldn't alter model outputs, it only serves previously computed KV states. though if the cached responses were generated by a slightly different model variant, that could create inconsistency. are you pinning exact model versions?
[02:48] Priya Kapoor: we pinned to redwood-3b-v1 but our infra team accidentally fell back to redwood-3b-v1a for a short window during a deploy.
[03:02] Maya Chen: ah that mismatch could explain a lot. model variant differences do show up as quality regressions in sensitive prompt-sets.
[03:16] Aisha Rahman: hmm okay, so next step: confirm the exact time window where the fallback happened and correlate with failure timestamps. we'll share logs.
[03:30] Tom Liu: quick security question — if we move to a dedicated pool or Private, how does KMS integration look? do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[03:44] Jordan Patel: yes for Dedicated and Private we support customer KMS; HSM support available via our enterprise compliance add-on. i'll pull the KMS integration doc and send it.
[03:58] Tom Liu: perfect, we need that for the procurement checklist.
[04:08] Elena Ruiz: note — i'll attach the security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts in the follow-up thread.
[04:18] Maya Chen: great. back to the regression — Jordan, can you outline the bisect plan and how you'll surface which paraphrases fail?
[04:30] Jordan Patel: sure — plan is: 1) run the eval on the canonical core set (the baseline), 2) run on each paraphrase batch in isolation, 3) compute delta per-example and aggregate. we'll flag top 20 regressions and include model logits and token-level alignments to diagnose hallucination triggers.
[04:50] Carlos Mendes: will you include temperature and top_p in the report? we had temp set to .2 but someone bumped it to .4 in a dev branch.
[05:03] Jordan Patel: yes we'll include full runtime config per run; that will show temperature, top_p, max_tokens and batching settings.
[05:15] Aisha Rahman: also curious about scoring — the spreadsheet shows a composite score we called 'safety_adj_score' — can we get per-metric breakouts?
[05:29] Jordan Patel: absolutely, we'll break down factuality, consistency, and guardrail flags. by the way, i noticed your guardrail rule that blocks any 12-digit numeric pattern — that generated some false positives for invoice IDs that match the pattern.
[05:45] Priya Kapoor: yeah we had complaints from the product team that legitimate invoice refs were being redacted.
[05:52] Maya Chen: typical tradeoff — tighter regex reduces risk but increases false positives. Jordan, thoughts on moving to a two-stage guardrail?
[06:05] Jordan Patel: propose a heuristic: stage one regex flag, stage two model-based classifier to verify true sensitive numeric leakage. classifier would be lightweight, run at the token-level, should keep latency impact minimal.
[06:20] Carlos Mendes: that sounds promising. what's the expected latency overhead? we need <120ms p95 on our critical path.
[06:29] Jordan Patel: initial estimate 8-12ms per request if hosted with batching, but depends on model and quantization. on Dedicated with int8 quant and continuous batching it may be lower.
[06:43] Aisha Rahman: okay keep that number in mind, our SLA target is p95 <120ms and cost target under $0.0009 per token.
[06:54] Maya Chen: i'll reflect the guardrail classifier cost into the cost model when i update it.
[07:02] Tom Liu: circling back to data residency — we process EU payments and need logs to stay within eu-west-1. how does Redwood handle region pinning for Private vs Dedicated?
[07:18] Jordan Patel: Dedicated can be provisioned in the region, Private gives you the control plane and you can pin compute to your VPC subnets. for hosted, we have region routing but logs may still be centralized unless you opt into dedicated retention. we'll detail choices in the doc.
[07:36] Priya Kapoor: is there a way to encrypt logs at rest with our KMS keys?
[07:42] Jordan Patel: yes for Private and Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS for encrypting both artifacts and audit logs.
[07:50] Aisha Rahman: excellent. back to evaluation: can we look at a couple of example failure transcripts?
[07:58] Maya Chen: Jordan, do you have top failures on hand?
[08:05] Jordan Patel: yep pulling the top five from the run — sharing screen... (minor screen shuffle) ok first sample, payments_prompt_042: prompt asks 'what's the merchant routing code for Santander UK', model answered with a 9-digit number and appended 'use at your discretion' — clearly hallucination.
[08:30] Carlos Mendes: in our labels that's a hard fail.
[08:34] Priya Kapoor: second sample?
[08:36] Jordan Patel: payments_prompt_117 — paraphrase with 'wire bank code for deposit', model returned a mix of bank name and an invented SWIFT. contextually wrong.
[08:47] Aisha Rahman: i'm noticing a pattern: questions that include non-standard phrasing or synonyms for 'routing' or 'swift' seem to trigger hallucination. maybe the paraphrase expansion pulled in low-quality crowd-sourced variations.
[08:59] Maya Chen: okay hypothesis: paraphrase noise + small model variant change + slight temp bump => regression. propose we do controlled bisect: start baseline canonical set + baseline runtime + baseline model variant, then add one variable at a time.
[09:18] Jordan Patel: agreed. we'll run 6 experiments: baseline, paraphrase batch A, paraphrase batch B, temp .2 vs .4, model variant v1 vs v1a, caching on/off.
[09:32] Carlos Mendes: that matrix should identify culprit. how long will that take?
[09:36] Jordan Patel: each run is ~20 minutes for 2k prompts at our current concurrency; we can parallelize on Dedicated but hosted will queue. expect 2-6 hours total depending on parallelism.
[09:49] Aisha Rahman: let's prioritize baseline vs paraphrase A overnight and have tentative results tomorrow morning.
[09:55] Maya Chen: noted. Elena, can you help coordinate?
[09:59] Elena Ruiz: yes i'll set the job and share links to run artifacts in the channel.
[10:04] Priya Kapoor: going back to guardrails: the false positive with invoice IDs — could we add an allowlist by known prefixes?
[10:13] Jordan Patel: yes allowlists are helpful. we suggest a hybrid: allowlist + regex + classifier so unknown patterns fall back to classifier decision. that reduces manual maintenance.
[10:25] Carlos Mendes: what's the operational cost of maintaining allowlists? we have thousands of vendor prefixes.
[10:31] Jordan Patel: you can supply a prefix table and we can put it into a fast-lookup store referenced by the guardrail. sync frequency can be daily. cost is minor but depends on size.
[10:42] Aisha Rahman: okay send an example implementation and we'll check how many prefixes we need to ship.
[10:47] Maya Chen: will do. also i want to call out a small regression the Redwood team saw internally with a recent quantization pass — it's rare but can alter tokenization alignment. that's why we recommend pinning a model hash for critical prompts.
[11:02] Priya Kapoor: sounds like pinning is a must for our payments flows.
[11:07] Tom Liu: procurement asks for explicit commitments on ability to pin and for audit logs per token request. can Redwood provide request-level audit logs with request_id?
[11:18] Jordan Patel: yes audit logs include request_id, model_hash, runtime_config, and optionally full prompt/response depending on retention settings and privacy options. we'll include a sample log schema.
[11:31] Aisha Rahman: that will help our compliance team.
[11:34] Maya Chen: ok we're at about 45 minutes — almost time. quick recap and owners: Jordan will run bisect and rerun latency microbench; Maya updates cost model; Aisha to provide labeled failures and pick critical prompt sets; Tom to share KMS/HSM requirements; Elena will post run links and attach security docs.
[11:53] Carlos Mendes: one more thing — for the bisect, can you include token-level attention heatmaps or is that too heavy?
[12:01] Jordan Patel: we can provide token alignments and top-k logits, attention heatmaps are heavier but possible for a sampled subset. we'll include them for the top 10 failures.
[12:13] Priya Kapoor: perfect.
[12:16] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone. will follow up with the shared artifacts and schedule the 30 minute triage on 2025-07-23.
[12:25] Aisha Rahman: thanks, talk soon.

Notes / artifacts shared:
- Eval spreadsheet: https://redwood-internal.s3/ss-pilot/eval-2025-07-16.csv (shared by customer)
- Run artifacts: link will be posted by Elena in thread
- Security whitepaper & SOC2 excerpt: attached by Elena
- KMS integration doc: Jordan to share (placeholder https://redwood.docs/kms-integration)

Transcript quirks: speaker overlaps at 09:36-09:49 some crosstalk, occasional mis-transcribed product name 'redwood-3b-v1a' as 'red wood three bee v1a' in auto-sub, numeric sequences sometimes garbled as 'one two three four' in the transcript.

End of meeting.
